fj_assumptions.source: pks+ E. coli carriage in healthy adults is commonly quoted around 20% (Nougayrede/Putze-era isolate surveys report the pks island in ~20-35% of commensal B2 E. coli); yersiniabactin (the confusable) is more common still, hence 0.35. Not re-verified against primary sources here.
cdt-bearing Enterobacteriaceae/Campylobacter carriage assumed 10%; the confusable pool (hlyA/stx/elt/typhoid-toxin cdtB) is broader, assumed 30%. Order-of-magnitude placeholders.

ESBL (largely CTX-M) faecal carriage in community cohorts varies enormously by region; 15% is a mid-range assumption. blaTEM in particular is near-ubiquitous in Enterobacteriaceae, hence 0.50 for the confusable pool.
